description: We are building an interactive, AI-powered fire safety dashboard using NASA's microgravity combustion data. Our goal is to summarize, rank, and interpret decades of space flame experiments to help engineers and astronauts prevent and extinguish fires on future Moon and Mars missions.
summary: FLARE is an SI-powered web dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and interprets NASA microgravity combustion experiments by flammability, data availability, and experimental relevance. It holds 27 source-linked records across 21 NASA investigations (BASS, Saffire, SoFIE, FLEX, ACME, SAME — now with verified observation records for SAME and ACME), in 7 workspaces: Research Agent, Mission Mode, IGNIS Scenario Lab, 3D Simulation Lab, Evidence Explorer, Experiment Comparison, and NASA Knowledge Base. Every answer names the investigation, the measurement, and the NASA source behind it — and shows where the evidence stops.
details:
Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Three.js, Recharts, Vitest. Research Agent: natural-language query. The AI model only selects existing record IDs and measurement keys via a strict JSON schema; scientific text is rendered deterministically from stored source fields, so the model cannot invent a number. Unknown citations are rejected. With no AI key configured, FLARE falls back to deterministic retrieval and says so on screen. Mission Mode ranks experiments deterministically by relevance, data availability, and flammability, and exports source-linked Markdown/JSON briefs. Experiment Comparison charts values only when both records report the same quantity in the same unit; unreported uncertainty is labelled "Not reported", never plotted as zero. Evidence Explorer shows tested-pair coverage and range-spanning records honestly; SAFFIRE-V atmosphere discrepancies are shown separately, not merged. 3D Simulation Lab is a conceptual illustration of chamber geometry — not CFD, not a measured flame shape. Roles: Karim El Assali — application development and engineering; Hamza Sailah — NASA experiment research and data curation; Mohamed Zaroual — software testing and product improvement suggestions. Backup demo deck: https://flare-space-apps.vercel.app/demo-deck.html Code: https://github.com/karimelassali/Nasa-flare-space-apps-2026 AI / SI disclosure: FLARE uses AI (NVIDIA NIM, Google Gemini, or OpenAI, server-side keys only) for evidence selection in the Research Agent and Mission Mode analysis. The model selects records and measurements only; all scientific statements are rendered from stored, source-linked fields. No free-form AI-generated numbers. Deterministic fallback applies when no provider key is configured. See docs/ai-disclosure.md in the repo.

Full per-record sources: see docs/data-provenance.md and the in-app "NASA Source" links on every record.
dataRefs: PSI Data Repository (primary source; BASS, Saffire, SoFIE, FLEX, ACME, SAME investigations)
NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) — SAFFIRE Table 1, NTRS 20180005168 (flame-spread 1.8 vs 2.3 mm/s; burn durations 420 vs 300 s)
NASA/TP-2015-216046, Table IX, NTRS 20150023456 — FLEX-008, 14.8 s droplet burn ending in disruption, not extinction
BASS-II rod study — 0.0385 mm/s rod-tip regression velocity; 13.5% oxygen minimum on a multi-test flammability boundary
